Description

Prostaglandins and other inflammatory mediators raise cAMP in nociceptors through adenylyl cyclase. cAMP binds the regulatory subunits of protein kinase A and frees its catalytic subunits, which phosphorylate TRPV1 and the sodium channel NaV1.8 and drive P2X3 receptors into the membrane, so the nerve ending fires at lower thresholds. After inflammation cAMP also signals through Epac and PKC epsilon, which prolongs this sensitisation.

Colour

Each block is coloured by its effect on pain, red where it raises pain and blue where it relieves it, and everything in it takes that colour, as it works for the block's result. The nucleotides and cofactors are olive. Drugs are yellow and classes of molecules white.

This block is red: PKA increases the currents of the channels.
